title: Role-Play Jailbreaks Defeat Semantic Intent Classifiers: Framing Compounds Detection Gaps

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Role-play jailbreaks are the most common real-world vector. Demonstrating that intent classifiers fail on framing directly informs classifier design priorities. Clear and actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a TF-IDF + SVM classifier is intro ML. Generating role-play variants of harmful prompts is manual/straightforward work. No GPU required for the classifier. Extremely accessible for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single experiment: train classifier on direct prompts, test on framed variants. Clear deliverable: detection accuracy by framing type. Well within 30 hours.
